top_story.headline: Quiet day: no standout filing across FARA, LDA or House and Senate disclosures
top_story.dek: The most notable item is a set of nominee ethics agreements with divestiture commitments.
paragraphs: No FARA registrations or terminations were filed, and the only new House stock-trade report is an unreadable scan. The OGE section below covers four nominees' ethics agreements with divestiture or resignation commitments.

sections.headline: Four Presidential Nominees File Ethics Agreements with Divestitures and Employment Resignations
paragraphs: Four nominees for positions at federal agencies submitted ethics agreements committing to divest financial holdings or resign from prior employment to address potential conflicts of interest. Additionally, eight routine filings were submitted by nominees across State Department, Treasury, Justice, and Education positions.

items: Francis J. Browne Jr., Under Secretary for Domestic Finance at the Department of the Treasury, filed an Ethics Agreement committing to divest his interests in SPDR Gold MiniShares Trust (GLDM), iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT), iShares Silver Trust (SLV), iShares Gold Trust (IAU), and SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) within 90 days of confirmation.

Dino LaVerghetta, nominee for Ambassador to the State of Kuwait at the Department of State, filed an Ethics Agreement committing to resign from his position with Sidley Austin LLP and to refrain from participating in matters involving the firm or his former clients for one year after resignation.

Scott E. Krueger, nominee for U.S. Marshal for the Northern District of Indiana at the Department of Justice, filed an Ethics Agreement committing to resign from his positions with the Indiana State Police and Alliance Security, Inc., with one-year post-resignation recusal periods.

Mark Priebe, nominee for Inspector General at the Department of Education, filed an Ethics Agreement committing to resign from positions with five sports officials associations, including the Rappahannock Valley Football Officials Association and Fredericksburg Volleyball Officials Association.

sections.headline: Five new lobbying registrations, led by AI legislation and digital-asset policy
paragraphs: Five new registrations were posted since 10/09/2026, alongside 307 total filings in the window, mostly third-quarter activity reports. Only the first page of 25 total filings was reviewed, so that count is the only statement made about the rest. Of those 25, nearly all were quarterly reports, including a cluster from Marla Grossman LLC for clients of its copyright-focused coalition. Source.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.
